source.title: On PAC-Bayesian reconstruction guarantees for VAEs
source.authors: Badr-Eddine Chérief-Abdellatif; Yu-Yang Shi; A. Doucet; Benjamin Guedj

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material are present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures reconstruction generalization for VAEs, but does not test any listed claim version about classifier memorization, architecture, optimizers, batch size, dropout effects in classifiers, sharpness measures, or memorized-example removal.
record.gate_note: The paper reports VAE reconstruction generalization and compares β-VAE with PAC-Bayes objectives. Its dropout discussion concerns prior learning within those procedures and does not isolate the effect of dropout on classifier test error. Figure 2 reports generalization-gap comparisons but does not provide recoverable numeric values in the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study derives and evaluates VAE reconstruction guarantees, which do not test V1–V8. Dropout is used in VAE prior learning, rather than classifier comparisons; flatness motivates the objective without a magnitude-aware sharpness ranking experiment. Mentions of classifier memorization and large-batch sharpness cite prior work.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors derive VAE reconstruction bounds and demonstrate objectives with competitive test reconstruction and small generalization gaps. They question the VAE KL term's relevance to reconstruction generalization. They also report that KL attenuation can improve reconstruction while making certificates vacuous, so tight certificates and best reconstruction need not coincide.
record.recipe_differences: The study evaluates VAE reconstruction objectives and PAC-Bayes bounds, rather than the classifier settings and interventions in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset (binarised MNIST versus Omniglot), PAC-Bayes objective and prior settings, β value, dropout during prior learning, and use of KL attenuation.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 2 reports smaller reconstruction generalization gaps for PAC-Bayes objectives than β-VAE baselines on both datasets; the best settings also improve test reconstruction loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In the tested feedforward VAE setup, PAC-Bayes training objectives can reduce reconstruction generalization gaps while maintaining competitive test reconstruction.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2022)
record.problems: The relevant generalization-gap comparisons are shown in figures without numeric values in the supplied text. The study evaluates binary-image VAE reconstruction, not the classifier behaviors specified in the versions.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows. Figure 2 comparisons are retained as aggregate figure-only rows because the text describes the aggregate result but does not state numeric curve values.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same recipe.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects on classifier held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with classifier generalization gaps and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized versus equally many random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative Figure 2 comparison is explicit in the text; unavailable numerical values do not make its direction indeterminate. The row states above concern their inability to establish any listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as network width exceeds the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers on images.
Dropout effects on classifier test error.
Magnitude-aware sharpness as a correlate of the training-test gap.
Effects of removing highly memorized training examples.
